glossary.metaTitle: Community glossary – feed, thread, moderation, presence explained
glossary.metaDescription: The key terms around community platforms, briefly explained: feed, thread, moderation, presence, embed, custom domain, roles, early access.
glossary.title: Community terms, briefly explained
glossary.lead: No jargon fog: the words used on this site and inside the platform – two sentences each.

terms.def: A place of your own where your members write, learn and meet – under your name, your design and your domain. Unlike a Facebook group, it belongs to you, not to someone else's network.
The chronological stream of posts and events in your community. It shows what's happening right now – and keeps people coming back.
A discussion whose replies sit indented under the original post. That keeps side conversations readable instead of tangled.
Everything that keeps content civil: reporting, hiding, restoring, enforcing rules. With us there's an AI second opinion – a human decides.
The live indication of who is reading, typing or replying. It makes a community feel inhabited instead of dead.
A block of your community placed inside another website – for example discussions under your blog posts. You don't have to migrate anything.
Your community runs under your address, e.g. community.yourcompany.com, instead of someone else's. With us that's intended for silo customers.
Who may do what: owner, admin, moderator, editor, viewer. Roles stop everyone from being able to do everything – and stop nobody from being able to do anything.
The individually switchable parts of the platform: discussions, moderation, pages, feed, courses, events. You take only what you need.
A block that exists but isn't released to everyone yet. We label it that way – instead of letting it look like a finished plan promise.
Content only signed-in members of your community can see. With us that's the default; publicly readable is a deliberate switch.
Your content and member data in a machine-readable package. It's the reason switching to us isn't a one-way street.

gdpr.metaTitle: Privacy at Pukalani – hosted in Germany, no ad tracking
gdpr.metaDescription: How we implement privacy technically: servers in Germany, no ad tracking, first-party sessions, export and deletion. Honest, without blanket seals.
gdpr.title: How we implement privacy
gdpr.lead: No seal, no marketing formula: here's where your data lives, what we don't do – and what we deliberately don't promise.
gdpr.disclaimerTitle: What this page is – and isn't
gdpr.disclaimer: This page explains our technology and operations. It is not legal advice and does not replace your community's own privacy policy – you need that for your own site, matching the blocks you switch on.

sections.title: Where your data lives
sections.text: On servers in Germany (Hetzner). We run the database self-hosted – there is no US cloud in your community's data path.

sections.title: What we don't do
sections.text: No ad tracking, no ads, no selling or sharing your data for advertising, no cross-site profiling. Your members are our users – not our product.

sections.title: Sessions instead of trackers
sections.text: For sign-in we use a strictly necessary first-party cookie (httpOnly, secure, sameSite) – no ad IDs, no third-party scripts in standard operation. Analytics is a switch, and ours is off by default.

sections.title: Your data is yours
sections.text: Export and deletion are built-in flows, not support tickets: full data export on request, full deletion including a prior snapshot so nothing disappears by accident.

sections.title: Transport and access
sections.text: Encrypted transport (TLS), separate keys for operations and migrations, server secrets never in the browser. Who sees what in your community is governed by roles – not by chance.

sections.title: Data processing agreement
sections.text: If you run a community with us, you are the controller and we process on your behalf. That requires a data processing agreement with us – talk to us and we'll sort it out before your community goes live.

gdpr.notPromisedLead: Others put seals here. We'd rather write down why there aren't any:

notPromised.why: Compliance depends on your configuration, your legal texts and your processes – not on our software alone. We provide the technology for it; nobody can sell you the seal.
Whether you need one depends on which services you enable on your site. In standard operation we set no advertising cookies – but that assessment belongs to your site, not to our marketing.
We back up regularly. We'll publish a commitment on recovery time and maximum data loss only once a documented restore test stands behind it.

gdpr.ctaLead: Try it free, export anytime, delete anytime.

circle.title: Pukalani vs Circle
circle.sub: The lean, privacy-close alternative — for communities that don't need a whole suite.
circle.intro: Circle is powerful: a broad suite, automations, scale. For small and mid-sized communities that's often more than they need – and pricier than they want. Pukalani bets on a few well-made building blocks, hosting in Germany and a predictable price with no transaction fee.
circle.whenThem: You need a broad suite with lots of automations, native mobile apps with push, or you're scaling to very large memberships with enterprise requirements. Circle gives you more surface there.
circle.whenUs: You want your own community home under your name, hosted in Germany, without ad tracking and without transaction fees – and you only want to switch on the blocks you actually use.

skool.whenThem: You like the gamified, highly guided approach, want zero setup worries, and it's fine that your community looks like Skool. Then Skool is fast and coherent.
skool.whenUs: Your community should look and be named like YOU, your revenue stays fully yours, and privacy isn't just a checkbox. Plus you want to embed discussions or events into your existing website.

story.title: A hole in the clouds.
story.intro: Far out in the Pacific lies Maui. High on the slopes of Haleakalā is a place called Pukalani. Its name is understood as an opening to the sky — a puka in the grey where light breaks through. That's where the idea for this platform was born.

strands.title: The hole in the clouds.
strands.text: Today's web is mostly clouded – full of tracking, ads, noise and closed networks where your community never truly belongs to you. Pukalani is the opening where the sun breaks through: a clear, calm place, without all the grey.

strands.title: The gateway to the sky.
strands.text: Puka and lani can be read as “an opening to the sky” — a door. And that's how the beginning should feel: you step through, and in sixty seconds your own community stands – no servers, no manual, no detours.

strands.title: Fertile ground.
strands.text: Pukalani sits in the highlands, on rich volcanic soil where things have grown for generations. That's our promise: a place where your community grows – your posts, your courses, your events, your people.

strands.title: A world of its own.
strands.text: Your community here is its own living world — sovereign, and entirely yours. It doesn't fade into someone else's network. What you build here belongs to you.

story.outro: Built by someone who wanted this platform to exist: honest, lean, privacy-first – without turning you or your members into the product. Pukalani is a special place. Pukalani.app is meant to be one too.
